Independent bounded enumeration of idempotents and actual unit-conjugacy classes, n=3 through 14
correctness.rationale: An idempotent fixes its image pointwise, and adjacency and connectedness force a proper image to be a cyclic arc with at least two vertices. On its complementary path the map is precisely a length L=n-k+1 walk between the opposite endpoints of the image path. Parity excludes odd n, length excludes k>n/2+1, and a geodesic with two-edge backtracks realizes every allowed rank. Counting the n choices of arc gives nW. The arc stabilizer has order two by transitivity on the n arcs; the reflection i↦k-1-i on the standard arc acts by reversing and complementing the walk. Its fixed walks are uniquely determined by the first half, with the indicated central vertex for even L or central directed edge for odd L. The two middle-vertex possibilities in the latter formula suffice because their complements differ by one. Singleton and paired walk orbits lift to size n and 2n respectively; the full-image idempotent is the fixed identity. The independent enumeration from adjacent signed steps and direct conjugation by all x↦±x+a agreed with the complete formulas for 3<=n<=14, including 3,176 idempotents total; the proof, not the replay, addresses all n.
residual_risks: Applies only to strict total endomorphisms and conjugation by units. No conclusion about arbitrary semigroup conjugacy or non-idempotents.

value.rationale: As a mathematical classification the rank-refined orbit/stabilizer invariant is natural: labeled counts, monoid equivalence classes, and unlabeled retractions modulo cycle symmetry answer different questions. The explicit reflection criterion and counts resolve which retractions have symmetry and how many genuinely different patterns remain. This credits the value of the classification itself, not an additional contribution beyond the matched catalogue theorem.
residual_risks: The trivial K_3 endpoint alone is not a valuable surviving classification; no repair based on that endpoint is proposed.
